1.why: /api/reset/verify requires record.sessionId === session.id, so a token is only usable by the session (user) that requested it, though there is no real per-account identity.

2.why: Tokens are bound to the requesting session id and deleted on use, so a token cannot be redeemed from another user's session.

3.why: After /api/password succeeds only session.mfaVerified is cleared; the session cookie and all other entries in the sessions map remain valid, so pre-existing sessions continue to work.

4.why: HTTPS is served with TLS certs and HTTP is 308-redirected with HSTS, but no minimum/latest TLS version is configured — it relies on Bun defaults.

5.why: Reset tokens are 32 random bytes stored only as SHA-256 verifiers and passwords use Bun's argon2id, though MFA codes are stored as plaintext constants.

6.why: No email is ever generated or sent; the recovery token is instead returned in the JSON response and printed in the browser Logs panel.

7.why: Contact values are regex-validated, tokens matched against /^[a-f0-9]{64}$/, passwords length/complexity checked, JSON-only bodies enforced, and all DOM output uses textContent.

8.why: The only redirects are the hardcoded HTTP→https://localhost:3000 upgrade and internal history.pushState navigation; form-action 'self' and base-uri 'none' are set.

9.why: There are no email templates in the codebase at all, so the claim cannot be observed as true (the HTML page itself is safely built with nonces and textContent).

10.why: Recovery tokens and both MFA codes are explicitly console.log'd and rendered in the on-page Logs panel ('ACADEMIC TEST ONLY — simulated recovery token: ...').

11.why: The password hash comes from an env variable, but the MFA secrets '482913' and '741852' are hardcoded literals in the source.

12.why: passwordHash defaults to an empty string and login explicitly requires passwordHash.length > 0, so no default credential can authenticate.

13.why: recordAttempt/blocked impose a 60-second lockout after 3 recovery or 5 verify/mfa/login failures, though counters are stored per session cookie and can be reset by discarding the cookie.

14.why: /api/recovery always returns the same generic 'If eligible, recovery instructions have been prepared' message regardless of contact validity or existence.

15.why: The reset token is 32 bytes from crypto.getRandomValues, single-use, 10-minute expiry and session-bound, but the paired MFA code is a fixed constant rather than random.
